info.name: WeAreDA Reseller Reference
info.description:
Every request in the WeAreDA reseller integration, in both directions.

    WeAreDA -> Reseller   folders 01-04 and parts of 10
                          calls INTO your commerce/ERP system
                          auth: X-API-Key (or bearer / basic / custom)

    Reseller -> WeAreDA   folders 05-08 and parts of 10
                          the signed webhook you call
                          auth: HMAC-SHA256 over the exact raw body

    Reseller -> WeAreDA   folders 00 and 09
    (management API)      the connect API and the read API on WeAreDA's
                          backend
                          auth: X-Reseller-Key

THREE DIFFERENT CREDENTIALS. They are not interchangeable.

Webhook requests sign themselves: a pre-request script builds the event,
serializes it ONCE, signs those exact bytes and sets X-WeAreDA-Signature,
X-WeAreDA-Event-Id and X-WeAreDA-Timestamp. The request body is the same
string that was signed.

Folder 00 registers the integration. integrationMode decides which of folders
01-04 apply to you at all - a receive_only reseller implements none of them and
still works, publishing through folders 05-08. Inbound webhooks work in every
mode.

Suggested order: 00 -> 01 -> 02 -> 03 (captures orderId) -> 05/07/08 -> 04.

Remember while you test: orders and stock are independent flows. Nothing in
folders 03 or 04 changes stock anywhere, on either side.

item.name: 00 - Integration Configuration (two scopes)
item.description:
Direction: Reseller -> WeAreDA management API (X-Reseller-Key), contract 1.1,
2, 6.1 and 7.1.

Configuration has TWO SCOPES, and two calls:

    INTEGRATION   POST /api/v1/resellers/me/integrations
                  once per (reseller, provider) - baseUrl, authType,
                  credentialScope, the credential, the webhook secret,
                  integrationMode, declaredCapabilities, syncConfig.
                  Changing it affects EVERY customer you serve.

    TENANT        POST .../tenants/{tenantId}/integration/attach
                  once per customer - orderDeliveryStatus, orderStatusWrite,
                  externalTenantId, and the credential at
                  credentialScope 'tenant'. Affects that one customer.

A field of the other scope is a 400 that NAMES where it belongs, in both
directions. POST .../integration/connect, which took both scopes in one body,
is gone: it answers 410 endpoint_removed.

    integrationMode    reads  order delivery  catalog
    query_and_send     yes    yes             pull      (default)
    receive_and_send   NO     yes             push
    query_only         yes    NO              pull
    receive_only       NO     NO              push

Inbound webhooks (folders 05-08) work in EVERY mode. The mode governs only
what WeAreDA does.

Run order: one create, then an attach (which captures wearedaWebhookUrl for
folders 05-08). A second create is 409 by design - restart the mock to try a
different mode.

Point wearedaApiBaseUrl at `npm run mock:weareda` (http://localhost:4000) to
run this folder without a real WeAreDA connection.

request.description:
INTEGRATION SCOPE, run ONCE. One integration per (reseller, provider),
shared by every customer you serve.

The default shape: WeAreDA reads your catalog on a schedule AND delivers
orders to you. You implement all four calls: GET /, GET /products,
POST /orders, POST /orders/{id}/cancel.

Nothing per-tenant belongs in this body - orderDeliveryStatus,
orderStatusWrite and externalTenantId are 400s here, naming the attach
call they belong to.

syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId (contract 4.3.2, 7) - a boolean, default
false, which is the behaviour every existing integration keeps.

true means WeAreDA NEVER delivers an order whose customer has no fiscal
identifier: the order is simply not yet eligible, and it is delivered
automatically - within a minute - once the tenant completes the contact.
Nothing is parked and nothing has to be re-queued.

That is the setting for a reseller that cannot invoice without a tax id.
Rejecting such orders on arrival is the wrong answer: a non-auth 4xx is not
retried, so it turns a waiting order into a manual-review ticket.

Unlike integrationMode (integration scope) and orderStatusWrite (tenant
scope), this one is a syncConfig option - it configures a delivery rule, not
the shape of the integration. A non-boolean value is 400 invalid_sync_config.

exec: pm.test('carries nothing per-tenant - that is the attach body', function () {

request.description:
WeAreDA pulls your catalog and never sends you an order. ordersWrite is
switched off in effectiveCapabilities, so an order never enters the
delivery queue at all - nothing is queued and later refused.

request.description:
Publish-only: nothing is ever called on your side. You still register a

item.name: 409 integration_exists - a create is not an upsert

request.description:
Run this after any successful create. POST /integrations creates; it never
upserts, precisely so it can never overwrite what your other customers are
running on. Change an existing integration with PATCH.

TENANT SCOPE, run once per customer. Only per-tenant settings live here,
and the response carries this customer's inbound webhook URL - captured
into the collection variable used by folders 05-08.

Attaching is idempotent per customer: an omitted field keeps its stored
value, so re-attaching never silently flips a setting you did not send.

The opt-in of contract 6.1: your order.status events then move the
CUSTOMER-FACING order status as well, along a ladder that only ever
advances (folder 05).

It is stored PER TENANT while integrationMode is stored per reseller, on
purpose: a mode change must never start rewriting a column the tenant's
staff edit, for every customer at once. It requires a mode that delivers
orders - with query_only or receive_only it is a 400.
Your integrations, and the customers attached to each one.

item.name: 2.3 GET one integration (read syncConfig BEFORE patching it)

request.description:
Read the stored syncConfig from here before you PATCH it: contract 7.1
REPLACES a named section whole rather than deep-merging it, so send the
current section back with your change applied.

item.name: 7.1 PATCH integration - allow-list a document host

request.description:
Partial edit at INTEGRATION scope - it affects every tenant of yours, and
the response says how many (affectedTenants, schedulesReconciled).

Merge rules (7.1): only the top-level keys you name are touched, a named
section is REPLACED whole, and null deletes a key. The merged result is
validated by the same rules a create would apply.

documentHosts takes BARE hostnames only - never a URL, port, path or IP
literal. This is also the fix for an invoice rejected as ssrf_blocked:
widen the list, then retry that operation.

item.name: 2.3 PUT credentials (rotation is never a side effect of an edit)

request.description:
The ONLY call that changes the connector credential. Under the removed
connect, a body that happened to carry credentials rotated the one every
customer of yours was authenticating with.

item.name: 2.3 PUT webhook-secret (one signing secret per reseller)

request.description:
Rotating the signing secret applies to EVERY webhook you send us
(contract 9). Sign the next event with the new value.

Echoes integrationMode, orderDeliveryEnabled and productsSyncMode for the
customer in the path.

exec: pm.test('echoes the three derived fields', function () {

The connection test IS a read, so under receive_and_send or receive_only

request.description:
The one breaking change of this contract (2.3, 9).

connect took BOTH scopes in one body against a tenant-scoped URL and
upserted the shared half, so connecting one customer rewrote the baseUrl,
auth type, credential scope, capabilities and syncConfig of all the
others - and rotated the shared credential as a side effect.

It was retired as a new PAIR of paths, never as a redefinition of the same
one: this answers 410 and names both replacements.

item.name: 400 - a TENANT field in the integration body

request.description:
orderStatusWrite is stored per tenant, so it belongs to the attach body.
The error names the call it belongs to rather than dropping it.

item.name: 400 - an INTEGRATION field in the attach body

request.description:
This is the mistake the old connect made invisible: a baseUrl sent while
attaching ONE customer used to be applied to ALL of them. Now it is a 400
naming POST /api/v1/resellers/me/integrations.

item.name: 400 invalid_request - orderStatusWrite on a mode without order delivery

request.description:
Run this after creating the integration in query_only or receive_only.
Those resellers never receive an order, so they have none to report a
status on and the flag could never fire.
A STRICT boolean. The string "true" is a 400, not a truthy value.

declaredCapabilities takes exactly six boolean keys and enables nothing.
integrationMode is a top-level field of this body.

syncConfig is a strict whitelist (contract 7), so a misplaced field there
fails loudly - unlike an unknown key at the top level, which is dropped in
silence. orderStatusWrite belongs to the attach body.

The mode DERIVES the catalog transport. A contradiction is a 400, not a
precedence puzzle: remove products.mode, or change integrationMode.

documentHosts takes up to 10 BARE hostnames - never a URL, a port, a path,
or an IP literal. Allow-listing an IP would route around the SSRF guard
the list exists to keep (contract 7, 9).

item.name: 201 but silently ignored - productsSyncMode at the top level

request.description:
The one that is NOT an error. productsSyncMode is a RESPONSE field: sent as
input it is dropped without a word, and the catalog transport stays 'pull'.
That silence is why this reference validates bodies locally before sending.

exec: pm.test('the top-level productsSyncMode changed nothing', function () {

item.name: 03 - Orders
item.description:
POST /orders - contract 4.3. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key, and ALWAYS returns the reseller order id.

Receiving an order changes NO stock (contract 6.4).

request.description:
Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

The delivered order. Note it carries NO external_order_id: WeAreDA identifies it by order_number + idempotency_key, and adopts YOUR id from the response.

Saves the returned id into the `orderId` variable.

The `customer` object (contract 4.3, added 2026-09) is OPTIONAL and ADDITIVE:
  - the whole key is OMITTED when the order has no contact;
  - customer.tax_id is NULL when the contact has no fiscal identification - the
    key is always present INSIDE customer, so you can branch on it directly;
  - tax_id.type is a FREE SHORT TOKEN, not an enum (CUIT, CUIL, DNI, CPF, CNPJ,
    NIF, NIE, CIF, RFC, EIN, SSN, VAT, TAX_ID, ...). An unknown value is normal:
    accept it verbatim, never normalise it, NEVER reject the order over it;
  - tax_id.country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2;
  - the values are a SNAPSHOT taken when the order was created (4.3.1). Do not
    expect them to match a later read of the customer, and never 'correct' a
    stored order from one. An order that arrived with no fiscal id may report
    one later - the snapshot freezes a value, not an absence.

If you cannot invoice without a fiscal id, set syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId:
true (4.3.2, folder 00) - WeAreDA then never delivers such an order, and
delivers it automatically within a minute of the tenant completing the contact.
Rejecting the delivery is the wrong answer: a non-auth 4xx is not retried.

The identifier below is deliberately fake. The sandbox MASKS it in every log
line and in GET /debug/orders (20-******78-9) and keeps the real value only on
the order it invoices against (11.8).

item.name: 05 - WeAreDA Webhooks
item.description: The signed inbound webhook - contract 6.1. One event type per HTTP request, always.

exec: // The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the EXACT RAW BODY BYTES that are sent.
// So we build the event, serialize it ONCE into `signedBody`, sign THAT
// string, and let the request body be exactly {{signedBody}}.
// Never re-stringify after signing - different bytes mean 401 unauthorized.
console.warn('webhookSecret is not set - WeAreDA will answer 401 unauthorized.');
const event = { type: 'order.status', id: eventId, order: { external_order_id: pm.collectionVariables.get('orderId') || pm.environment.get('orderId'), state: 'accepted' } };
// Serialize once. This exact string is what gets signed AND sent.
// Optional per contract 3.2; must be within the +/-5 minute replay window.
console.log('Deduped: this event id was already processed (contract 6.0).');
console.log('202 means QUEUED, not applied. Effects land shortly after (contract 6.0).');

request.description:
Direction: Reseller -> WeAreDA.

order.status (contract 6.1). ONE event per transition, each with its own event id.

TWO columns. integration_status always moves; orders.status - the customer-facing
one - moves only when the tenant registered orderStatusWrite: true (folder 00).

  state                                    integration_status  orders.status
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  accepted | acknowledged | ack            accepted            confirmed
  shipped | fulfilled                      completed           shipped
  delivered | completed                    completed           delivered
  cancelled | canceled                     cancelled           cancelled
  returned | return | refunded |
    not_delivered | undelivered            returned            refunded
  rejected | failed | error                manual_review       (unchanged)
  anything else                            NOT MAPPED          (unchanged)

shipped and delivered COLLAPSE to completed, so orders.status is derived from the
RAW state, never from integration_status. fulfilled maps to shipped, not delivered:
the cheaper wrong guess, since the ladder discards a lower rung arriving later.

LADDER      draft -> pending -> confirmed -> processing -> shipped -> delivered
            Only ever ADVANCES. A lower rung after a higher one is ignored.
EXCEPTIONS  cancelled, refunded - apply from ANY rung at ANY time.

This event NEVER changes stock - not even shipped or delivered.

request.description:
Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

Means WeAreDA's registered credential does not match your RESELLER_API_KEY. Not retried: the integration goes to manual_review.

Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

Run it as many times as you like: the order count never grows. Check GET /debug/orders.

The `customer` object (contract 4.3, added 2026-09) is OPTIONAL and ADDITIVE:
  - the whole key is OMITTED when the order has no contact;
  - customer.tax_id is NULL when the contact has no fiscal identification - the
    key is always present INSIDE customer, so you can branch on it directly;
  - tax_id.type is a FREE SHORT TOKEN, not an enum (CUIT, CUIL, DNI, CPF, CNPJ,
    NIF, NIE, CIF, RFC, EIN, SSN, VAT, TAX_ID, ...). An unknown value is normal:
    accept it verbatim, never normalise it, NEVER reject the order over it;
  - tax_id.country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2;
  - the values are a SNAPSHOT taken when the order was created (4.3.1). Do not
    expect them to match a later read of the customer, and never 'correct' a
    stored order from one. An order that arrived with no fiscal id may report
    one later - the snapshot freezes a value, not an absence.

If you cannot invoice without a fiscal id, set syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId:
true (4.3.2, folder 00) - WeAreDA then never delivers such an order, and
delivers it automatically within a minute of the tenant completing the contact.
Rejecting the delivery is the wrong answer: a non-auth 4xx is not retried.

The identifier below is deliberately fake. The sandbox MASKS it in every log
line and in GET /debug/orders (20-******78-9) and keeps the real value only on
the order it invoices against (11.8).
